age.evidence: Male Wistar rats (220-250 g, 8-10 weeks old)

sex.evidence: Male Wistar rats (220-250 g, 8-10 weeks old)

dosing.evidence: The powder was mixed with sterile normal saline and administered orally by gavage (2 mL/kg) to the animals at three doses of 10, 100, and 250 mg/kg ... every other day for 14 days.

day_night_flipped.evidence: The animals were housed under a 12 h/12 h light/dark cycle (direction not specified).

assays.assay_description: Three-chamber sociability and social novelty test; social preference phase (empty box vs. stranger 1) followed immediately by social novelty phase (stranger 1 vs. stranger 2). Each phase recorded for 10 min. Outcomes: time spent in chambers, exploring time, sociability index, social novelty index.

setup_restrain.evidence: Animals freely explored chambers; behavior was recorded by a camera.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard three-chamber test; no food present in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard three-chamber test; no water present in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral assessments were started one day after the last dose.

sample_size.evidence: randomly divided into four experimental groups (n = 10/group)

outcomes.summary: P. azurescens at 100 and 250 mg/kg reduced exploration of the stranger rat and decreased both the sociability index and social novelty index, indicating dose-dependent disruption of social interaction and social recognition. The 10 mg/kg dose did not alter these measures.
outcomes.statistics: Sociability index F(3,36)=6.418, p<0.01; Social novelty index F(3,36)=10.06, p<0.001; Exploring Stranger 1 F(3,36)=8.91, p<0.001; Exploring Stranger 2 F(3,36)=5.958, p<0.01.
outcomes.evidence: The sociability index was lower in P. azurescens 100 and 250 mg/kg than in the control group (p<0.05 and p<0.01, respectively). Treatment with P. azurescens at 100 and 250 mg/kg doses reduced the social novelty index versus the control (p<0.001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: time in chambers, exploring time for empty box, exploring time for stranger 1, exploring time for stranger 2, sociability index, social novelty index

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Totals over 10-min phases; no within-session time-course analysis.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Social investigation (exploring/sniffing stranger rat) was quantified.

B5_social.evidence: Stranger rat was placed in lateral chamber enclosed by a box (barrier).

B6_cognitive.evidence: Social novelty preference phase requires recognition memory of the first stranger.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: All variables were scored using a chronometer by a blind experimenter.

E6_spatial.evidence: Three distinct chambers separated by walls.

E7_social_context.evidence: Stranger rat enclosed in a box during recording.

D1_continuity.evidence: Two phases run back-to-back on a single test day.

D2_session_duration.evidence: 10 min social preference + 10 min social novelty = ~20 min total session.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug baseline for this assay.

D5_followup.evidence: Test conducted ~24 h after the last dose.

assays.assay_description: Plus-shaped plexiglass maze with two open and two closed arms. Animal placed in center facing an open arm; 5-min recording. Measures: open/closed arm time and entries, total arm time, total arm entries, anxiety index.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard EPM; no food in apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard EPM; no water in apparatus.

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral assessments were started one day after the last dose.

outcomes.summary: All doses of P. azurescens (10, 100, 250 mg/kg) decreased open-arm time and entries, increased closed-arm time and entries, and increased the anxiety index compared to control, indicating anxiety-like behavior at all tested doses.
outcomes.statistics: Open-arm time F(3,36)=25.98, p<0.001; Open-arm entries F(3,36)=26.19, p<0.001; Anxiety index F(3,36)=34.77, p<0.001; Total arm time F(3,36)=3.441, p<0.05; Total entries F(3,36)=1.446, p=0.246.
outcomes.evidence: All doses of P. azurescens decreased open-arm time (p<0.001) and open-arm entries (p<0.001) ... All P. azurescens doses increased the anxiety index compared to the control (p<0.001).

B1_num_measures.evidence: open-arm time, open-arm entries, closed-arm time, closed-arm entries, total arm time, total arm entries, anxiety index

B4_ethological.evidence: Zone preference time is a spatial measure, not an ethological behaviour.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Innate avoidance test; no learning/memory required.

E2_shelter.evidence: EPM closed arms are part of apparatus design, not a shelter.

E6_spatial.evidence: EPM arms are open extensions of a central platform.

E7_social_context.evidence: Only the focal animal in the apparatus.

assays.assay_description: FST in a cylinder tank (50 cm height x 30 cm width) filled with water (23-27 degC). 15-min habituation swim on day 1; 5-min test swim on day 2. Measures: swimming, climbing (active), immobility (passive).

setup_habituation.evidence: The experiment consisted of a habituation phase on the first day (15 min of swimming) and a testing phase (5 min of swimming) on the second day.

setup_restrain.evidence: FST cylinder is treated as a restraint apparatus per rubric.

food_restriction.evidence: No food in apparatus during test.

water_restriction.evidence: No drinking water accessible during test (animal is submerged).

time_to_assay.evidence: Behavioral assessments were started one day after the last dose.

outcomes.summary: P. azurescens at 100 and 250 mg/kg decreased active behavior (swimming + climbing) and increased passive behavior (immobility) versus control, indicating dose-dependent depressive-like behavior; 10 mg/kg had no effect.
outcomes.statistics: Active behavior F(3,36)=10.38, p<0.001; Passive behavior F(3,36)=10.9, p<0.001.
outcomes.evidence: Administration of P. azurescens 100 and 250 mg/kg decreased active behavior (swimming and climbing) (p<0.05 and p<0.01) and increased passive behavior (immobility) (p<0.05 and p<0.001) compared to the control.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Active behavior (swimming + climbing reported jointly) and passive behavior (immobility).

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility is not an ethological behaviour per rubric.

E8_food_water.evidence: No accessible food/water (water is the test medium).

D1_continuity.evidence: Habituation swim on day 1 (15 min) and test swim on day 2 (5 min).

D2_session_duration.evidence: Habituation phase on day 1 = 15 min of swimming (longest single session).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Day 1 habituation swim + day 2 test swim = 2 days animal was in the apparatus.

D4_baseline.evidence: Day-1 habituation data not reported as analyzed baseline.

D5_followup.evidence: Behavioral assessments started one day after the last dose.

judge_notes: Three candidates agreed on three behavioural assays: Three-Chamber Test, Elevated Plus Maze, and Forced Swimming Test. No merges or drops required.
Psychedelic compound entered as Psilocybe azurescens whole mushroom powder (not isolated psilocybin); the paper administered dried mushroom material, not a purified compound.

Three-Chamber D2 set to 15-60 min because the test consists of two consecutive 10-min phases (~20 min total within a single continuous session), per qwen's interpretation; glm and gptoss scored only one 10-min phase.

FST D3 scored as 2-7 days (2 days): habituation day 1 + test day 2 both involve the animal in the apparatus and constitute distinct recording days for this assay (per rubric example for fear conditioning train+test).
FST setup_restrain = yes per rubric explicit listing of FST cylinder as restraint apparatus (overriding glm/gptoss 'no').
Housing day_night_flipped set to not_reported (high confidence) because the paper states a 12:12 cycle but does not specify direction — informative silence.
DOI 10.1002/jnr.70107 taken from the article URL string visible in the markdown (onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/jnr.70107).
